description:
RBAC v2 design + permission inventory is a cross-functional security foundation project to move Redwood Inference from coarse, feature-gated access controls to a consistent, fine-grained authorization system that can support enterprise-grade requirements (custom roles, least privilege, auditability) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals:
- Produce a complete inventory of sensitive actions across the Redwood control plane, console, API, data-plane operational tooling, and admin surfaces (including "break-glass" and support-only operations).
- Define RBAC v2 primitives (resources, actions, scopes) and a small set of default roles (e.g., Org Admin, Billing Admin, Security Admin, Developer, Read-only, Support/Impersonation) with clear separation of duties.
- Implement a unified permission-check library + policy evaluation path used consistently across services (API gateway/control plane/console backends), with strong test coverage.
- Deliver migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with backwards compatibility (feature flags), clear rollout/monitoring, and customer-facing documentation where needed.
- Establish ongoing governance: how new sensitive actions are added, reviewed, tested, and documented; and how evidence is produced for audits (SOC 2/ISO) and customer security reviews.

Scope:
- In-scope: control plane APIs, console endpoints, audit-logging context (include actor/role/decision), admin tooling used by support/SRE, private deployment installer/admin flows, and policy bundle packaging.
- Out-of-scope (initially): data-plane token-level inference authorization beyond tenant/project scoping, and deep refactors of identity provider integrations (SSO/SAML) except where needed to map groups/claims to roles.

Key stakeholders:
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin (exec owner for product security), Kevin Osei (audit log/export alignment), Hanae Suzuki (secure defaults + private templates).
- Security leadership/GRC: Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO) for risk acceptance and priority; Olga Petrov (GRC) for control mapping and evidence needs.
- Platform Control Plane: Ethan Park (eng lead) and Kaitlyn Nguyen (authz implementation lead).
- Product/PM + Enterprise readiness: PMs for Console/Private/Hosted API (review role UX and admin workflows) and Solutions Engineering/CS (feedback from enterprise evaluations).
- SRE: review operational break-glass workflows and incident-time access patterns.

Phases & timeline (typical 8–12 weeks):
1) Permission inventory (2–3 weeks): catalog endpoints/actions; classify sensitivity; identify existing gaps/inconsistent checks.
2) RBAC v2 model & policy format (2–3 weeks): resources/actions taxonomy, role definitions, policy bundle versioning.
3) Implementation (3–5 weeks): shared authz library, service integrations, console changes, tests, audit log enrichment.
4) Migration + rollout (2–4 weeks): dual-write/dual-evaluate, feature flags, customer comms for Private/Dedicated, deprecate RBAC v1.
5) Governance (ongoing): change management, checklists for new endpoints, periodic access review hooks.

Constraints and risks:
- Performance overhead of checks on hot paths (must be low-latency and cacheable).
- Backwards compatibility and avoiding accidental privilege loss (especially for enterprise admins and support workflows).
- Policy distribution for Private deployments (offline/air-gapped) and version skew.
- Auditability: every authorization decision should be explainable and attributable in logs.

Deliverables:
- A permission inventory (sheet) + sensitivity classification rubric.
- RBAC v2 design spec + ADRs for key decisions.
- Policy bundle repo updates + integration PRs across services.
- Runbooks for break-glass/support access, and internal policy/governance docs.
- Customer-facing enablement artifacts for security reviews (as needed).

files.description: Published overview: RBAC v2 goals, terminology (resource/action/scope), default roles, and how authorization is enforced across control plane + console + private deployments; includes diagrams and ownership.
Process doc: how to enumerate sensitive actions, classification rubric (P0/P1/P2 sensitivity), required metadata per action (service, endpoint, actor types), and review workflow.
Default role matrix with separation-of-duties notes, examples (billing vs security vs ops), and mapping guidance for SSO group claims.
Step-by-step migration plan: dual-eval strategy, feature flags, rollout stages by tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), safe rollback, and customer comms checklist.
Spec for adding authorization decision context to audit logs (actor, role, policy version, allow/deny, reason codes), with examples and retention considerations.
ADR describing chosen policy schema (YAML/JSON), versioning strategy, evaluation semantics (deny-overrides vs allow-only), and rationale vs alternatives.
Engineering standard: where and how to enforce checks (gateway vs service), error codes, logging requirements, and unit/integration testing expectations.
Restricted internal policy/runbook defining break-glass and support impersonation access: approvals, time-bounded grants, monitoring, and audit evidence.
Working spreadsheet (sheet): full list of actions/endpoints, sensitivity rating, current check status (missing/partial/ok), and proposed RBAC v2 action names.
Draft design doc with open questions, rough diagrams, notes from reviews, and links to Linear epics/PRs; less polished than Confluence.
Implementation sketch for shared authorization library: interfaces, caching approach, expected call sites in services, and test harness plan.
Notes exploring how policy bundles are shipped/updated for Private (including air-gapped): installer hooks, signatures, and version skew handling.
PM/Design collaboration notes: console UI for role assignment, custom roles vs defaults, warnings for high-risk permissions, and admin onboarding copy.
Table-driven audit of console backend endpoints and current auth gaps; includes quick annotations from engineers during inventory.
Launch checklist: monitoring, alerting, runbook readiness, known risky permissions, comms plan, and post-launch access review tasks.
SRE notes: incident-time operational actions requiring elevated access, proposed break-glass workflow changes, and constraints for on-call tooling.
Epic: RBAC v2 + permission inventory (project container). Goals/non-goals, milestones, and sub-issues for inventory, policy format, service integrations, and migration.
Implement permission inventory crawler/script to enumerate API routes and annotate sensitivity; outputs seed data for the inventory sheet.
Define RBAC v2 resource/action taxonomy and naming conventions; includes examples for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
Build shared authz library (Go/TS depending on services) with policy evaluation, caching, and standardized error handling.
Integrate RBAC v2 checks into control-plane service endpoints (tenant/project admin, keys, model rollouts); includes acceptance criteria and tests.
Console: add role assignment UI + guard sensitive pages/actions; includes UX review steps and feature flag strategy.
Audit log enrichment: include authz decision context and role info; ensure event schemas are stable for SIEM export.
Private deployments: policy bundle distribution and update mechanism (installer integration) + documentation.
RBAC v1->v2 migration plan implementation: dual-eval, metrics, rollout playbook, and deprecation timeline.
PRD: Enterprise roles & permissions (RBAC v2) with customer requirements, success metrics, and phased rollout across Hosted/Dedicated/Private tiers.
Design ticket: Console IA + UI patterns for role management, permission warnings, and audit log visibility for authorization failures.
Threat modeling task: identify privilege escalation paths, impersonation risks, and required mitigations in RBAC v2 evaluation + admin flows.
PR: Introduce RBAC v2 core types (resource/action/scope) and a central authorization middleware hook in the control plane service.
PR: Add standardized authz error responses (403 reason codes) and structured logging fields for allow/deny decisions.
PR: Implement policy cache + per-org invalidation with metrics for cache hit rate and policy evaluation latency.
PR: Add RBAC v2 checks to API key management endpoints (create/rotate/revoke/list) with tests validating least-privilege behavior.
PR: Guard Dedicated capacity admin endpoints (autoscaling policies, GPU pool config) with new permissions; includes rollout flag.
PR: Add audit log fields for authz decisions (policy_version, role_ids, decision_reason) and update event schemas.
PR: Console backend: enforce RBAC v2 on sensitive routes (billing, org settings, SSO config) and add integration tests.
PR: Break-glass workflow plumbing (time-bounded elevated session) with explicit audit events and admin-only controls.
PR: Dual-evaluation mode (RBAC v1 + v2) with shadow-deny metrics and dashboards for migration safety.
PR: Remove/disable legacy RBAC v1 checks for a first set of endpoints after successful shadow period; includes rollback instructions.
PR: Add initial RBAC v2 policy bundle v0.1 (default roles + permissions) with schema validation and versioning notes.
PR: Add private-deployment policy bundle packaging (signed artifact) and docs for updating bundles during upgrades.
PR: Exporter update to include new authz decision fields; update mappings for common SIEM targets and add backward-compatible handling.
PR: Update internal/external docs stubs: roles overview, permission errors, and admin guidance for Private customers.
PR: Add conformance test suite that ensures new endpoints declare a permission and have an authz check wired (CI enforcement).
Thread coordinating permission inventory scope and sensitivity rubric; includes back-and-forth on what counts as "sensitive" for enterprise audits.
Thread: platform team clarifies where to enforce checks (gateway vs service) and concerns about performance overhead.
Thread: review of ADR proposal for policy evaluation semantics (deny overrides vs allow-only) and implications for debugging.
Thread: discussion of break-glass design, who can grant access, and how to audit/alert on usage.

Thread: internal support asks why certain admin actions started returning 403 in staging; engineers explain feature flag/shadow mode.
